sample_unit: trials emulated (three independent agent runs each)

links.outcome: Error between EHR-derived and published log hazard ratios before vs after local Bayesian calibration
links.effect: Calibration reduced mean absolute error from 0.567 to 0.224 log-HR (60.5% reduction) in leave-one-out validation; out-of-distribution AVERROES error fell from 0.379 to 0.051 (86.5%).
links.quote: In pooled leave-one-out validation, calibration reduced mean absolute error from 0.567 to 0.224 log–hazard ratio (60.5% reduction) and achieved 100% empirical coverage of 95% posterior predictive intervals across held-out trials (4/4).

links.outcome: Systematic shift between trial evidence and local EHR-derived effect estimates
links.effect: Posterior institution-specific shift consistently positive across folds (median 0.364–0.580), indicating systematic attenuation of DOAC benefit in the local EHR beyond literature-expected disagreement.
links.quote: The posterior institution-specific shift was consistently positive across folds (median 0.364–0.580), indicating systematic attenuation of DOAC benefit in the local EHR beyond literature-expected disagreement; residual heterogeneity was moderate (median 0.199–0.264).

screen.reason: Empirical study evaluating an autonomous LLM agent workflow for trial emulation, testing whether hierarchical Bayesian calibration can adjust agent-generated EHR trial emulation discrepancies to published trial results.

primary.practice: Bayesian calibration of EHR-derived agentic estimates to published RCT results
